en: Think, forty companions;
Know this worth of mine.
Your lion will raise the battle shout;
Fear no death; raise the conflict!
The pressure of Judgment Day,
Your fathers' graves, forty companions,
We are among those who have seen it.
With Ajybay and Bakay renowned,
While lion Manas is here,
Let it be an unforgettable deed,
The conflict the magnanimous man unleashes!
Sharing booty, companions in gathering,
Dying together, companions in faith,
The one you will fight is Khan Shooruk.
Lest we become divided,
My finest men, join hands!
If we submit to Shooruk,
Ajybay and Bakay, the two,
Let us put forward as mediators.
Becoming clean of the dark faith,
Separating him from the unbelievers, making him a stranger to them,
Showing boundless valor,
Bringing him into the faith of Islam,
Let us make him a Muslim.
If he will not heed these words of mine,
If he will not enter the Muslim faith,
Let us bring extraordinary slaughter.
Of that damned Shooruk's people,
Ravaging many,
Let us wage abundant combat.
Drawing bows to shower arrows like rain,
Upon Shooruk, whose life has fled,
Let us turn a cold countenance.
Clashing and fighting,
Let us settle down to besiege him!
Let us drive off his abundant livestock.
If he will not heed our words,
If he will not give what we desire,
Upon Shooruk, who boasts of his might,
Sweeping down and drawing bows,
Let us trample down upon his head.
Making him say, “Master, I submit!”
Let us scatter his four kinds of livestock!
Sweeping straight toward him,
Grappling and raising conflict,
Let us return in battle.
If he rages, let us beat out
His devil that has run so far astray.
If by chance he comes to terms,
If by chance he listens to reason,
Let us say, “Heed our words!
What we desire, what we have in mind,
Without fighting, Khan Shooruk,
Prepare and give to us!”
If he does not heed what is said,
If he shows his strength and defies us,
Bolting his gates tight,
If he swells with pride, saying, “I am khan,”
Before the mouth of his gate,
Turning our winged steeds and making them prance,
If obstinacy seizes him,
Let us make them all crawl, sparing none.
Let us utter our taunts,
Taking many as booty,
Let us treat him like a sheep in humiliation.
His abundant wealth and many livestock,
Let us take as booty and return!
If he defies us, let us fight,
Let us beat out utterly
That swaggering Shooruk's
Devil from its furthest hiding place.
Let us work out how to bring him to reason;
If he refuses to heed reason,
Come, forty mighty men,
Let us raid Shooruk's people.
“This is what battle is,” we shall say;
If Shooruk defies us,
Let us sound trumpets and shawms,
Thrusting spears and firing shots,
Let us return raising dust in battle.
Even traveling six months without rest,
My ranks of winged steeds will endure.
Bakay blessed by Khizir, and Ajybay,
These men, heading the forty companions,
Are the wings on which I circle and fly.
Your fathers' graves, forty companions,
All forty of you are my wings.
Not forty retainers, but forty friends,
If a warrior is speared, though you spear him,
Let the name belong to Manas!
All forty of you yourselves,
My kinsmen on whom I rely,
Let my single life become forty;
From the one creator God
This is what I ask.
Twins of matching age,
When their temper is provoked,
Oceans who can shatter nations.
Dust rises from your passing,
Lion courage, hearts of stone,
My dear forty companions,
Your voices drive out men's souls.
While you forty companions are here,
Gold-collared, impenetrable to bullets,
I intend to clothe myself.
If my strength permits,
The enemy who says he will fight,
I intend to attack.
Taking a spear of black steel,
However many gather, five by five,
I intend to bind them in bundles.
While the mighty men stand beside me,
What ears have heard and eyes have seen,
With lands that do not yield,
I intend to wage war.
All my mighty comrades,
I stand eating sliced rump meat.
Whom ears have heard and eyes have seen,
Enemies boasting of their might,
I intend to make them face me.
As I ponder to myself,
Of the red gorge wrapped in haze,
I intend to be the ridge.
While the mighty men stand in numbers,
Not merely China, but the nations,
I intend to be their master.
My champions, my lions,
Sharing death, united in life,
My warriors who stand beside me,
If a formidable enemy rises shouting,
Let me send you all against him, forty companions.
Muslims who heed words,
Let me subdue through words;
Unbelievers who know no faith,
Let me subdue by force!
Lying or standing, forty companions,
I always rely on you as my support.
Whom Solomon's hand never reached,
Mortals dwelling undisturbed,
Overcoming them and confounding them,
While you mighty men are here,
I intend to call them to account.
Your fathers' graves, forty mighty men,
Encountered from the unseen,
To this head blessed by Khizir,
Friends until Judgment Day,
Found coming from forty places,
The lone blood-stained Kyrgyz man's
Honor was shielded by them.
While you forty companions were here,
Migrating in haste from Altay,
I settled in Talas, dwelling on the land.
If my forty companions raise their cry,
I deem Crimea too little, taking it captive.
Keeping Keng-Kol as my dwelling land,
Of the teeming Chinese,
I shall take its khanate captive.
Until this head of mine perishes,
There is no escape from fighting.
While the blood-stained man is safe,
Mark this, forty companions,
There is no way to go apart!
Ajybay, Bakay, warrior Kyrgyl,
Among the forty companions,
My champion who has worn out many shirts,
Your elders Kyrgyl and Bakay,
If they do not die from this world,
I shall raise as khans
All of you over the face of the earth,
My hungry lions,
My exceptionally wild, outstanding men,
My warriors who can shatter the world,
If the enemy we desire appears,
If he will not heed what is said,
If he will not listen to your words,
Fighting without turning aside,
Let us pass onward in wrath.
Without leaving the tiniest remnant,
Let us all perish in slaughter!
Breaking stone and making a road,
Toward the arrogant enemy
Let us advance to measure our strength.
With not one of us remaining,
Let us fall in mutual slaughter.
Let us not draw back from doom,
Let us not turn back from death!
Your fathers' graves, forty mighty men,
With your formidable Manas beside you,
With Kyrgyl and Bakay at your head,
Of death and suffering,
Could anyone be afraid?
Birth is certain, death is certain;
Are there people who do not die?
Consider, forty companions:
One of the seven days is death;
Can there be fear of death?
Named Shooruk, a mighty khan,
His courage lofty, his wrath fierce,
We are going to fight him.
His name has spread through the world;
A formidable khan of weighty spiritual power,
A steel door, a gateway,
I reckon he cannot be.
Facing Shooruk,
Unless we go and call him to account,
If that khan heeds words,
Let us tell him words he will hear.
Making them all Muslims,
Let us set them in order and return.
Cleansing them of the dark faith,
Estranging them from the unbelievers' faith,
For his daughter with five braids,
Becoming marriage kin, driving livestock,
Folding our arms respectfully, chewing rich fat,
Let us meet face to face and depart.
If he faces us and fights,
Leveling his ancestral fortress,
Let us slaughter them all and depart.
If he happens to make trouble,
If by chance fighting breaks out,
Let us ravage his possessions;
Let us bring destruction in this manner.
Speaking taunting, harsh words,
Within his gate,
Let us enter trailing our spears.
That damned Shooruk's
Desires let us discover.
If Khan Shooruk acts crookedly,
If he makes the slightest move,
I will raise the cry, forty companions.
Level your spears and grip them firmly;
Sweep over them in splendid fashion.
With not one of you left standing,
Perish in the slaughter!
If black guns thunder,
If thick battle breaks out,
If you flee, you will pay for it!
If fierce guns crack,
If by chance you take fright,
If you panic, you will pay for it!
We are going against a formidable enemy;
We shall besiege the court.
When we go to besiege the khan,
If you make the slightest false move,
If by chance you turn aside,
If your conduct appears bad,
I shall bring terrible hardship.
All of you forty companions,
Your elders headed by Kyrgyl,
I shall take your heads with my sword!
If your faithful service is shown,
Over Crimea and China
I shall raise you as khans.
Listen, you white-bearded elders;
Forty companions, all of you, listen!
Who set the grassy earth ablaze,
